sentence: Amlodipine is a prescription medicine from the group called calcium channel blockers.
note: NHS page title/summary: prescription calcium channel blocker for high blood pressure and angina.

sentence: Doctors use it to treat high blood pressure, which is also called hypertension.
note: NHS: used for high blood pressure.

sentence: The NHS says that bringing blood pressure down lowers the risk of serious problems such as heart attacks and strokes.
note: NHS: used to reduce risk of serious problems like heart attacks and stroke.

sentence: It is also used for chest pain caused by heart disease, known as angina.
note: NHS: used for chest pain caused by heart disease (angina).

sentence: The NHS says amlodipine works by widening the blood vessels.
note: NHS: works by widening blood vessels.

sentence: This lowers blood pressure and makes it easier for the heart to pump blood around the body.
note: NHS: lowers blood pressure and makes it easier for the heart to pump blood around the body.

sentence: Most adults can take amlodipine, and the NHS says many children can too.
note: NHS: most adults and children over 6 can take it; number omitted deliberately.

sentence: You can take it at any time of day, but the NHS suggests keeping to about the same time each day.
note: NHS: can take at any time but try to make it around the same time each day.

sentence: If side effects bother you, the NHS says your doctor may be able to prescribe a different medicine.
note: Summary of the NHS how-and-when page: doctor may prescribe a different medicine if side effects bother you.

sentence: The NHS says common side effects are usually mild and last only a short time.
note: NHS side-effects page: common side effects are usually mild and short-lived.

sentence: They include swelling in the ankles, feet and legs, headaches, dizziness, sleepiness, a pounding heartbeat, flushing, feeling sick and tiredness.
note: NHS side-effects page list: oedema of ankles/feet/legs, headaches, dizziness, sleepiness, palpitations, flushing, nausea, bowel changes, tiredness.

sentence: Swelling in the ankles, feet and legs is one of the most common of these effects.
note: Search summary: ankle swelling is one of the most common side effects; NHS lists oedema among common effects.

sentence: The NHS About amlodipine page says these effects usually improve after a few days.
note: Summary of the NHS About page: usually improve after a few days; contrasts with the other NHS wording that some can last longer.

sentence: For swelling, the NHS advises raising your legs when you are sitting down.
note: Search summary: NHS advice is to raise legs when sitting; blended across NHS pages, attributed to the side-effects page.

sentence: Some side effects ease after a while as your body gets used to the medicine, but others can last longer.
note: Search summary quoting NHS: some side effects should ease after a week or so as the body gets used to it, others can last longer; the week figure omitted.

sentence: The NHS says that if you feel dizzy you should not drive, ride a bike or use tools or machinery until the dizziness passes.
note: NHS: do not drive, ride a bike or operate tools or machinery until dizziness passes.

sentence: Serious side effects are rare, according to the NHS.
note: NHS: serious side effects are rare.

sentence: Severe stomach pain can be a sign of an inflamed pancreas, and yellowing of the skin or eyes can be a sign of liver problems.
note: NHS lists severe stomach pain (pancreatitis) and yellow skin/eyes (liver problems) as rare serious effects.

sentence: Anyone with these signs should contact NHS 111 or a GP the same day.
note: Route-to-care sentence added by author per house rules; the retrieved text did not give the route for these two.

sentence: The NHS says to call 999 if your lips, mouth, throat or tongue suddenly swell, or if you have difficulty breathing, because these can be signs of a serious allergic reaction.
note: NHS: sudden swelling of lips, mouth, throat or tongue, or breathing difficulty, needs 999.

sentence: Chest pain that does not go away after a few minutes, or chest pain that is new or worse in someone who already has angina, also needs a 999 call because it could be a heart attack.
note: NHS: chest pain that does not stop after a few minutes, or new/worse if you have angina, needs 999 as it could be a heart attack.

sentence: The NHS says that large amounts of grapefruit or grapefruit juice can raise the level of amlodipine in your body and make side effects worse.
note: NHS and UK leaflet: grapefruit/juice can increase amlodipine in the body and worsen side effects.

sentence: A UK patient leaflet gives the same warning.
note: Leaflet (emc pil.4717): grapefruit and juice can raise blood levels of amlodipine.

sentence: The NHS says alcohol can add to the blood-pressure-lowering effect of amlodipine.
note: Search summary: alcohol can increase risk of low blood pressure; page attribution blended between NHS main and side-effects pages.

sentence: This can bring on sleepiness, dizziness or headaches, so the NHS suggests limiting how much you drink.
note: Same summary: limit alcohol as it can cause sleepiness, dizziness or headaches.

sentence: Amlodipine can also interact with a statin called simvastatin.
note: Amlodipine SmPC: interaction with simvastatin.

sentence: The UK product information says amlodipine raises the amount of simvastatin in the body, so doctors limit the simvastatin dose in people who take both.
note: SmPC: co-administration increased simvastatin exposure and recommends limiting the simvastatin dose; numbers omitted.

sentence: The reason given is a higher risk of muscle damage with higher simvastatin doses.
note: Summary: limit due to increased risk of skeletal muscle toxicity.

sentence: The NHS says amlodipine is not suitable for everyone.
note: NHS: not suitable for everyone.

sentence: You may be advised against it if you have had an allergic reaction or serious side effect from amlodipine or a similar medicine.
note: NHS who-cannot-take list.

sentence: The same list names low blood pressure, heart failure, a recent heart attack and a past narrowing of a heart valve.
note: NHS list: low blood pressure, heart failure, recent heart attack, history of heart valve narrowing.

sentence: UK patient leaflets say people with severe low blood pressure should not take it.
note: Leaflets: do not take if you have severe low blood pressure.

sentence: In pregnancy, the NHS says amlodipine is not usually recommended because similar medicines have better safety information, but it may be used if other options have failed.
note: NHS main page: not usually recommended in pregnancy, safer similar medicines, may be used if other options fail.

sentence: The NHS pregnancy page says there is not a lot of information on its safety but it is not thought to be harmful to the baby, so the pages differ in tone.
note: NHS pregnancy page tone; flagged as a difference between NHS pages.

sentence: For breastfeeding, the NHS says small amounts pass into breast milk and have not been known to cause side effects in breastfed babies.
note: NHS pregnancy/breastfeeding page.

sentence: It says taking it is fine if a doctor or health visitor confirms the baby is healthy.
note: Same page.

sentence: Yes, swelling in the ankles, feet and legs is one of the common side effects listed by the NHS.
note: NHS list of common side effects.

note: Raise legs advice; see section note.
